meta.name: Check shipping documents against SharePoint instructions with OneDrive and Claude

name: Check shipping documents against shipping instructions in OneDrive, then chase originals via Outlook

nodes.name: Every morning
nodes.notes: The daily scan. Every shipment folder under the root is checked, and the chase clock runs from here.

nodes.name: A file lands in a shipment folder
nodes.notes: The same folder id as in Configuration; a trigger runs first and cannot read it. A file arriving in any shipment subfolder re-runs the scan for that shipment alone, so an approval request goes out within minutes rather than next morning.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes: Everything an operator changes lives here, and nothing an operator changes lives anywhere else. The folder id, the site id and the desk address are the three that have to change before this runs.

assignments.name: disclaimer
assignments.value: This message concerns the documents for the shipment named above and was sent by the document control desk. Please reply to the desk, not to this address, if anything in it is wrong.

assignments.name: ai_notice
assignments.value: The document values quoted above were read from the files by an AI system and compared with the shipping instruction by fixed rules. Nobody has reviewed the reading yet; check the document before acting on it.

nodes.name: List shipment folders
nodes.notes: One subfolder per shipment, named with the shipment reference. The root itself holds nothing else that matters.

nodes.name: Pick the shipments in scope
nodes.notes: All of them for the morning scan. Only the one a file landed in when the trigger fired. A trigger that did not run cannot be read, which is how the two cases are told apart.

nodes.name: Read the shipping instructions
nodes.notes: The Shipments list, whole, once per run. One row per shipment: the expected values the documents have to agree with, and the worklist columns this workflow fills. A plain call to the same API the SharePoint node wraps, with the same credential, because the native read drops the columns on older node versions.

nodes.name: Read the document requirements
nodes.notes: The Document requirements list, whole, once per run. One row per document per contract: whether it is required, whether an original is, and which fields on the Shipments row it has to agree with.

nodes.name: Join folders to rows
nodes.notes: Each folder in scope with its row and the requirement rows for its contract. A folder with no row is refused by name.

nodes.name: Find drafts and originals
nodes.notes: The two subfolders, by name. The folder is the state machine: a file in drafts is a draft, a file in originals is an original, and nothing else about the file says which.

nodes.name: Classify by filename
nodes.notes: The filename decides what a file is, through an alias table: BL, bill of lading, HBL; phyto; COO, certificate of origin; and so on. The newest file wins when two name the same document. A file nobody can classify is reported, never guessed.

nodes.name: Check completeness
nodes.notes: The free verdict. Required rows against files present, per phase. No model is involved, and this alone catches the commonest cause of a rejected presentation: a document that is simply not there.

nodes.name: File to base64
nodes.notes: Without this the model receives the string filesystem-v2 where a document should be, and every reading comes back not stated. Binary lives on disk; the Code node sandbox cannot resolve it.

nodes.name: Build the reading request
nodes.notes: The prompt is generated from the requirement row: exactly the fields it names, as written on the page. The model is never asked whether the document is right.

nodes.name: Ask the model
nodes.notes: The one call to a model. The endpoint and the model name are Configuration values. A failed call is a document that could not be read, recorded as such, and never a pass.

nodes.name: Read the answer
nodes.notes: Named values back out of the reply, then the comparison: normalised text containment for words, tolerance for numbers. The rules live in src/engine/compare.js and are unit tested there.

nodes.name: Compose the verdict
nodes.notes: Status, next step, what is missing, what disagrees, whether to chase, and who hears. Identical facts produce identical sentences, every morning.

nodes.name: Update the worklist row
nodes.notes: Matched on Title, the shipment reference. Only the worklist columns are written; the expected values a person typed are never touched. The ai_generated column carries the Article 50 envelope while the discrepancies column quotes what a model read, and is empty otherwise.

nodes.name: Append to the log
nodes.notes: Append only. A status change and a chase each get a line; a quiet morning gets none.

nodes.name: Tell the desk
nodes.notes: Internal. Approval requests with the form link, folders with no row, files nobody could classify, discrepancies. Stays inside the company. A discrepancy notice carries the Article 50 line and an X-AI-Generated header, because it quotes what the model read.

nodes.name: Chase the counterparty
nodes.notes: The only node in the workflow that reaches outside the company. Nudges and escalations for originals, with the disclaimer from Configuration on the bottom of every one. Remove the Outlook credential and the worklist still updates; only the sending stops.

nodes.name: Approval form
nodes.notes: The link in the approval request opens this with the reference already filled in. It can also be opened from a bookmark and typed.

values.placeholder: The approval is recorded against this name
Optional. Goes on the log line.

parameters.formDescription: Approving sends the request for originals to the counterparty on the shipment row and starts the chase clock. Rejecting records who rejected and why, and sends nothing.

nodes.name: Configuration (gate)
nodes.notes: Everything an operator changes lives here, and nothing an operator changes lives anywhere else. The folder id, the site id and the desk address are the three that have to change before this runs.

assignments.name: disclaimer
assignments.value: This message concerns the documents for the shipment named above and was sent by the document control desk. Please reply to the desk, not to this address, if anything in it is wrong.

assignments.name: ai_notice
assignments.value: The document values quoted above were read from the files by an AI system and compared with the shipping instruction by fixed rules. Nobody has reviewed the reading yet; check the document before acting on it.

nodes.name: Read the shipment row
nodes.notes: The whole list; the gate picks its row by reference in code. A reference nobody knows then reaches the refusal with an answer instead of stopping the form.

nodes.name: Read the document requirements (gate)
nodes.notes: Which originals to ask for is a requirement question, so the rows are read here rather than copied onto the shipment.

nodes.name: Check the gate
nodes.notes: The row has to exist, be ready for approval, and not be approved already. Pressing twice is harmless: the second press learns who pressed first.

nodes.name: Record the decision
nodes.notes: The name comes off the form field, the time off the clock, and the phase moves from drafts to originals. From here the daily scan checks the originals folder and chases.

nodes.name: Request the originals
nodes.notes: Goes to the counterparty on the row, after a person has pressed approve and never before. Reject sends nothing.

parameters.content:
## Shipment document control

### Who's it for
Supply chain and logistics teams whose shipments move under bills of lading, phytosanitary and origin certificates that have to agree with the shipping instruction before they are presented.

### How it works
One OneDrive folder per shipment, with drafts and originals inside. Every morning, and whenever a file lands, files are named from their filenames and the required documents are checked for presence. A model reads the fields each requirement row names out of each draft; fixed rules compare them with the Shipments row. A named person approves on a form; originals are then requested and chased.

### How to set up
1. Create the three SharePoint lists from the CSVs in the repository.
2. Create a shipments folder on OneDrive: one subfolder per shipment, each holding drafts and originals.
3. Put the folder id, site id and desk address in both Configuration nodes and the folder id on the OneDrive trigger.
4. Attach OneDrive, SharePoint and model credentials. Outlook is optional.

### Requirements
n8n 1.90 or later, one Azure app registration, a model credential.

---

Automatiqa Lab by Aleks Sidorecs
Detailed workflow description lives here: https:///www.automatiqa.io/ship-doc/

### Two ways in

The morning scan checks every shipment folder. The OneDrive trigger re-runs the same path for the one shipment a file just landed in, so an approval request goes out within minutes.

**Configuration is the only node an operator edits.** The folder id, the site id and the desk address must change; everything else has a working default.

### Whose folder is this

Folders are named by shipment reference and paired with the Shipments row of the same Title. The row is the shipping instruction: consignee, vessel, ports, weight, marks. The requirement rows for its contract say which documents must be there and which fields each has to agree with.

**Document types are rows, never branches.** Adding a document is a row on the requirements list, not a change to a node.

A folder with no row is refused by name to the desk. Nothing in it is checked.

nodes.name: Lane: What is in the folder

parameters.content:
### What is in the folder

`drafts/` and `originals/` inside each shipment folder. The folder is the state machine: where a file sits says what phase it is in.

Files are named from their filename through an alias table: BL, HBL, bill of lading; phyto; COO, certificate of origin; invoice; packing; weight; quality, COA; fumigation; insurance; ICO. The newest file wins when two name the same document. A file nobody can classify counts for nothing and is reported to the desk.

**Completeness is free.** Required rows against files present, no model involved. This alone catches the commonest cause of a rejected presentation.

### The model reads

Each present draft is downloaded and sent to the model with a prompt generated from its requirement row: exactly the fields named there, copied as written, null where absent. The model is never asked whether the document is right.

The endpoint and the model name are Configuration values. The body is shaped for the Messages API; another provider needs a proxy that speaks it.

A call that fails is a document that could not be read, and the row says so. It is never a pass.

### The rules decide

Text agrees when the instruction value appears in the document value after normalising case and punctuation. Numbers agree within the tolerance on the requirement row. Every failure names both values.

**The `next_step` column is the worklist.** Readable text, not a code: `awaiting draft phytosanitary certificate`, `discrepancy: bill of lading consignee ...`, `chase originals, day 4`, `ready to present`. Sort the Shipments list on it and you have the morning.

Only worklist columns are written. The values a person typed are never touched. The log gets a line on every change and every chase, and nothing on a quiet morning.

### Who hears

The desk hears about what it has to act on: a shipment ready for approval, with the form link; a discrepancy; a folder with no row; a file that needs renaming. Not about every scan.

The counterparty is chased for originals from the day after the chase interval, and the escalation address is copied once the escalation interval has passed. **Chase the counterparty is the only node that leaves the company**, and the disclaimer from Configuration is on the bottom of every message it sends.

No Outlook credential? Both nodes fail quietly and the worklist is still current.

### The gate

The human gate. Nothing before this point decides anything, and no request for originals goes out without a press.

The row has to exist, be ready for approval, and not be approved already. Pressing twice is harmless: the second press learns who pressed first. The name on the form is the name on the record.

### The record

Approve writes who and when, moves the shipment to the originals phase, logs it, and sends the request for originals to the counterparty on the row. From then on the morning scan watches the originals folder and chases.

Reject writes who and why, logs it, and sends nothing. Telling the counterparty what was wrong is a conversation, not a template.
